ults.config.title: Ultimate Storage
ults.config.local_only: Saves this client's config/ults.json only. Run /ults reload on an integrated server to apply it; a remote dedicated server cannot be changed from here.
ults.config.language.tooltip: Language the server uses for its command replies and screens.
ults.config.language.invalid: Choose one of the bundled languages.
ults.config.item_visibility.tooltip:
What a player sees until they pick a mode of their own.

Right-click the status book in the storage screen to switch. Show everything is offered only while it is this default, or to a player who may manage the storage.

Show everything — every item and category, stored or not.
Survival obtainable — what survival can obtain, always; anything else while it is stored; empty categories are hidden.
Available now — what the storage can hand over right now, crafting included; empty categories are hidden.
ults.config.storage_mode.tooltip:
Where the stored items are. Applied by /ults reload.

Void storage — every input container feeds a store of the server's own.
Remote storage — no store of its own: items are read from and taken out of the bound containers, while their chunks are loaded.
ults.config.permission.tooltip: Vanilla permission level (0-4) needed to bind containers or areas, to remove bindings, to toggle the highlight and to reload. Listing the bindings is open to everyone.
ults.config.multi_block_containers.toolt:
Block ids whose connected blocks together form one container, for modded containers that give every part an inventory of its own.

Vanilla chests, trapped chests and copper chests are recognised on their own.

Example: modid:big_chest
ults.config.multi_block_containers.inval: Enter a block id that exists in this game.
ults.config.max_bindings.tooltip: How many containers the storage may bind. 0 means no limit.
ults.config.drain_interval.tooltip:
Ticks between two drain visits of the same input container: 1 means every tick.

A larger value saves server time on a huge warehouse, at the price of items waiting a little longer in the input container. Hoppers that feed an input container are emptied every tick regardless, so a bound container keeps taking items in as fast as its hoppers push them.
ults.config.crafting.tooltip:
Whether a withdrawal may craft what it is short of.

Crafting needs the matching station in stock — a crafting table or a stonecutter — and uses it without consuming it. The station is chosen per recipe, so a recipe a stonecutter does in fewer operations is preferred while one is stored. Only the missing part is crafted.

Recipes the game works out while it runs — dyeing, fireworks, banners, copying maps, repairing — stay out of it.
ults.config.allow_full_inventory.tooltip:
Whether a withdrawal may go ahead when the backpack cannot hold everything it asks for.

On — what does not fit is dropped on the ground, so a player with a full backpack can still empty a stock out.
Off — the withdrawal screen refuses the request instead.
ults.config.special_stack_rule.tooltip:
When two stacks of one item are the same kind of thing, which is what lets them pool into one row.

The item and its name are the precondition either way: a plain sword and an enchanted one are two kinds, and so are two swords with different names.

Same components — every component has to agree, durability included. This is the game's own rule for two interchangeable stacks, and a stack handed over is always the very one that was stored.
Same tooltip — what a player reads on them has to agree, so two swords worn differently pool while a different enchantment never does. A stack handed over is then a stack of that kind rather than the exact one that was stored.

Used everywhere two stacks are compared, in every category.
ults.config.special_bundle_slots.tooltip:
How many stored stacks one bag holds.

Past this count the least recently stored stack is destroyed as new ones arrive, so a busy server can never fill a bag up.

A bag screen shows %s stacks to a page, so the default of %s stacks fills %s pages.
ults.config.special_filter_mode.tooltip:
What happens to the stacks the item list below names.

Off — nothing is taken out of the storage.
Keep full durability — only a worn one is taken out; one at full durability is kept.
Filter everything — taken out whatever state it is in.

A plain stack of the same item is never touched, and neither is a stack a player renamed: naming something is a deliberate act. Enchanting is not renaming, so enchanted gear is still filtered.
ults.config.special_filters.tooltip:
Item ids the filter takes out of the storage. Nothing is filtered unless it is named here.

Only a stack a category cannot show is at stake: a plain iron sword pools with its kind and never reaches this list, and a stack a player renamed is left alone.

Example: minecraft:iron_sword
ults.config.special_filters.invalid: Enter an item id that exists in this game.
ults.config.save_success.detail: The local file was checked and written. Run /ults reload to apply it.
ults.config.save_failed.detail: The local file was not written.
ults.special.empty.filter: Nothing in this bag matches the search.
ults.gui.bag.title: [%s] Bag
ults.config.take_all_stacks.tooltip:
How many stacks one "take everything" takes at most. The default of %s is one backpack's worth.

A bigger value takes more per click, and the storage hands it over a tick at a time anyway, so this decides how much one click is for rather than how fast it leaves.
ults.config.take_all_rate.tooltip:
How many items one "take everything" moves per tick while it runs. The default of %s is one stack a tick.

This is what keeps a warehouse-sized stock from being one enormous operation: a take-everything pours its stock out at this rate until it is done, so the server never has to move a pile in a single tick. Raising it empties a stock faster and asks more of the server for those ticks.
ults.take.done: Took everything: %s out of the storage.
ults.take.failed.backpack: your backpack has no room left.
ults.take.failed.empty: the storage has nothing left to hand over.
ults.config.allow_take_all.tooltip:
Whether players may empty a stock out with "take everything" at all.

With it off the offer is not there: the hint on a row and on a bag's status book leaves the line out, and the clicks that would start one do nothing — no screen, no sound and no message.
